lastCompletedStory.title: Isolate the four builder-based signal-bearing supervisor test files onto fixture configs

nextStoryContext: US-004 (CAM-420) applied the identical GENERIC_SUPERVISOR_CONFIG_PATH configPath-fixture idiom from US-003 to the 4 smaller signal-bearing supervisor test files that already had their own Partial<RunSupervisorOptions>-based makeBaseOpts/overrides builder: test/supervisor/pause-halt.test.ts, test/supervisor/pause-resume.test.ts, test/logging/spawn-resolution.test.ts, test/supervisor/loop-model-resolution.test.ts. Each file got its OWN independent module-level mkdtempSync fixture dir (not a shared import from loop.test.ts, to avoid cross-file lifecycle coupling), a `[backend]\nimplementer = "claude"\n` project.toml written into it, an afterAll cleanup, and the `configPath: 'configPath' in overrides ? overrides.configPath : GENERIC_SUPERVISOR_CONFIG_PATH` default line appended after the `...overrides` spread inside each file's makeBaseOpts return object. loop-model-resolution.test.ts was the only one of the four with chdir-based tests: its withClaudeShapedCodexCwd helper (used by the AC2 and AC3 tests) and one inline process.chdir-staged test (the AC4 'absent codexModelsCacheReaderFn' test) each got an explicit `configPath: undefined` sibling key added directly inside their makeBaseOpts({...}) call literal, preserving their deliberate real-cwd-relative-resolution coverage against their own staged project.toml fixture. The remaining AC4 test in that file ('claude-backed dispatch never invokes the injected cacheReader') deliberately got NO override -- it now resolves via the new shared fixture instead of the repo's live project.toml, which is exactly the fix: this was one of the 11 pre-existing residual fails under a committed codex backend (per US-003's handoff), and it is now green under that condition. The stale loop-model-resolution.test.ts:132-136 docstring claiming readPhaseBackend/readPhaseModel are 'not injectable through RunSupervisorOptions' was rewritten to say they ARE 'fixture-injectable via RunSupervisorOptions.configPath (CAM-420, US-004 ...)', since that seam now exists project-wide (was already false since US-001 of this PRD, but this story is the first to touch this file's docstring). Verification: `bun test` on those 4 files individually is 18 pass / 0 fail; full `bun test` is 5633 pass / 0 fail (unchanged count from US-003 -- no tests added/removed, only fixture wiring); `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun run check:all` fully green (no file-size/coverage/debt-marker/dead-code/dup ratchet triggered by this diff -- patterns.md is not budgeted by file-size-budget.json). Dress rehearsal (AC4, exact US-003 recipe: git worktree of committed HEAD, project.toml patched to add `implementer = "codex"` under [backend] -- NOT replacing the existing `name = "claude"` global default, since the per-phase key wins per readPhaseBackend's precedence -- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `bun test` with an emptied HOME): dropped from the documented 11 residual fails (post-US-003 baseline) to EXACTLY 6 fails, all in events.test.ts (3: worker-start->worker-end->result->tokens lifecycle, handoff-schema-warning, no-events-when-logEvent-absent) and ensure-worker-pane.test.ts (3: all 3 'implement branch' respawn-pane-targeting tests), matching this story's AC4 prediction byte-for-byte. Neither of those 2 remaining files has a Partial<RunSupervisorOptions>-based overrides builder to hang the configPath default off (per this story's own PRD notes, these were split into a separate follow-up, US-005, because their mechanics differ: builder-less files need per-literal call-site edits rather than one default line in a shared builder). Any future story touching events.test.ts or ensure-worker-pane.test.ts to eliminate the last 6 codex-coupled fails should follow US-005's approach, not this story's builder-default idiom.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Pure test-fixture DI-isolation story, mirroring US-003 of this same PRD exactly: no new external library surface introduced. RunSupervisorOptions.configPath already existed (US-001 of this PRD) and was already wired into readPhaseBackend/resolvePhaseModel; this story only threaded the pre-existing seam into 4 more test files' local makeBaseOpts factories.
